model_annotation: Figure 2 displays negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between the baseline Mistral-v0.2 model and the same model further fine-tuned on each of six specialty datasets. The chart is a horizontal bar plot with specialty terms—Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics—listed along the vertical axis, arranged in a fixed order from top to bottom. The horizontal axis represents negative log-probabilities, scaled linearly from 0 to approximately 2.5, with tick marks at intervals of 0.5. Each group of bars corresponds to one specialty, and within each group, two bars are shown: a lighter-colored bar representing the baseline Mistral-v0.2 model and a darker-colored bar representing the model fine-tuned on that specialty. The color coding indicates that each bar within a group is generated by the same model (baseline or fine-tuned) across all specialties. For each specialty, the fine-tuned model exhibits a lower negative log-probability (i.e., higher log-probability) for clinically relevant tokens compared to the baseline, indicating improved alignment with clinical language. The bars are sorted by specialty in the same order as listed in the table, and no specific bar is visually emphasized or annotated. The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning shifts the model’s token probability distribution toward the clinical domain, with the magnitude of improvement varying slightly across specialties.
